description.narrative: " The National Legislature of Liberia has the constitutional mandate to hold the Executive Branch of government accountable for proper management of public finances. However, during the fourteen years of civil conflict, there was no functioning legislature in Liberia. As a result, the legislature is confronted with significant capacity challenges in fulfilling its public finance oversight responsibilities as Liberia moves from the transitional post-conflict recovery phase to laying the foundations for long-term development. These challenges are reflected in (i) the significant delays in budget scrutiny and timely approvals of annual budgets which together have been affecting the effectiveness of, and predictability in budget execution, impacting service delivery efficiency; and (ii) significant backlog of review of audit reports and audited accounts submitted by the General Auditing These capacity weaknesses in the functioning of the legislature, particularly the Ways and Means / Appropriations Committees and the Public Accounts Committee, have severely limited the effectiveness of the oversight role of the Legislature. It is against this background that the Government considers it imperative for measures to be implemented to address the serious capacity deficiencies and to make the Legislature a more functional institution in its oversight role. Towards this goal, a delegation of the Liberia Legislature approached the World Bank office in Liberia to seek support under an IDF grant facility for activities that will help strengthen the Parliamentary oversight of the budget and public accounts committees as an integral part of effective public expenditure management and financial accountability. This IDF grant proposal is in response to this request, but focusing on the strengthening of the PAC arm of parliament. The overarching development objective of this grant is to enhance executive accountability in the use of public resources through a methodical process of parliamentary oversight. The expected outcomes are: "" an enhanced accountability regime through revitalization of the process of legislative oversight, "" increased effectiveness of PAC, supported by streamlined processes and adequately resourced Secretariat, and "" an established enabling environment for PAC to better understand and interact with its primary stakeholders within Liberia, and outside Liberia such as the West African Association Public Accounts Committee Association (WAPPAC) to better deliver on its accountability oversight role."
